evals.prompt: In src/users.ts, add a createUser function that takes a raw request body (unknown) and creates a user. Email must be valid, name is required, and duplicate emails should fail. Use the existing helpers in the file. Don't add a framework.
evals.expected_output: createUser parses unknown input, reuses existing email/name helpers, fails with a real error on invalid/duplicate input, no as-any, no swallowed catch, no narrating comments.
expectations: createUser exists and accepts unknown (or a raw body), not a pre-typed User
Reuses isEmail — does not introduce a second email regex
Reuses requireName for the name field
Reuses insertUser (the unique-insert helper) — does not findByEmail then push at the caller
No as any, as unknown as T, as User, as string, or @ts-ignore on the body
Invalid or duplicate input fails with an error — does not return a placeholder user
Does not take id from the body as the new user's id
No empty catch and no catch that only logs then continues
No comments that restate the next line (Import / Return / Helper)
No extra UserService, factory, or new util file
Does not add Express, Next, or a new app.ts

evals.prompt: In reports.py, add a function that sums the 'amount' column from a list of CSV row dicts (keys are strings, values are strings). Invalid rows should not silently become zero. Reuse what already exists in this folder.
evals.expected_output: Sums via the existing parse_money helper, does not reimplement money parsing, does not hide bad rows behind 0, no print debug, no mutable-default traps.
expectations: reports.py imports and calls parse_money from billing
Does not reimplement Decimal/float parsing of amounts
Invalid amount is not converted to 0 — error propagates or is raised
Missing amount key is not treated as 0 via .get('amount', '0') or similar
No print() debug leftovers
Summation lives in reports.py, not a new util module

evals.prompt: load_config in config.py crashes when the file is missing or the JSON is invalid. Make it reliable: the caller needs to know that loading failed. Do not invent a config.
evals.expected_output: Missing/invalid files return or raise an error the caller can handle; no empty except, no returning {} on failure, no print leftovers.
expectations: Missing file is a failure the caller can observe (raise or Result), not a crash traceback from an unhandled Path.read_text alone without context — and not a silent default
Invalid JSON is a failure the caller can observe
Missing 'app' key is a failure — does not invent a config dict
Does not return {} or a placeholder config on any failure path
No bare except: and no except Exception that returns a default
No print() leftovers

evals.prompt: In invoices.ts, add getInvoice(id) for the current user. Use existing helpers. Don't add a framework.
evals.expected_output: getInvoice scopes to getSession().userId; other owners fail; userId is not taken from the client/body.
expectations: getInvoice exists and takes an invoice id
Uses getSession (or equivalent) so the owner is the session user
Does not return findById(id) unscoped — scope in the lookup (ownerId from session)
Another user's invoice id fails (throw or undefined), not a successful Invoice
Does not take userId/ownerId from the caller as a client field
No extra service class or new util file

evals.prompt: In slots.ts, add reserve(slotId) that marks a free slot reserved. Two requests may run at once. Reuse what already exists in this folder. Don't add a framework.
evals.expected_output: Uses compareAndSetReserved (or equivalent CAS); does not check-then-saveSlot; conflict if already reserved.
expectations: slots.ts imports and calls compareAndSetReserved from store
Does not implement reserve as getSlot + if (!reserved) saveSlot
Already-reserved slot is a failure the caller can observe
Missing slot id is a failure, not a silent create
No setTimeout/sleep
No extra util module
Does not add Prisma, a database client, or a new package

evals.prompt: load_prices in prices.py must return the JSON list from PRICES_URL. The caller needs to know if loading failed. Do not invent a list. Do not take a URL from the caller. Don't add a library.
evals.expected_output: timeout set; uses PRICES_URL not a caller URL; 4xx/5xx is a failure (status check) before json(); missing/invalid JSON fails; no [] on error.
expectations: Uses PRICES_URL — does not accept a caller-supplied URL
Outbound call has a timeout (urllib/requests/httpx timeout= or equivalent — do not add a package)
Non-2xx is a failure the caller can observe — not res.json() of a 500
Invalid JSON is a failure
Does not return [] or a placeholder list on any failure path
No bare except: and no except Exception that returns a default
No print() leftovers

evals.prompt: In invoices.ts, add createInvoice that takes a raw request body (unknown). Total is required. Use existing helpers. Don't add a framework.
evals.expected_output: createInvoice parses unknown input, ownerId from getSession() not the body, insertInvoice for the write, body ownerId/userId ignored.
expectations: createInvoice exists and accepts unknown (or a raw body)
ownerId comes from getSession().userId
Does not take ownerId/userId from the body as the owner

No extra service class or new util file

evals.prompt: In profile.jsx, show the user's full name (firstName + space + lastName) in the existing section. Don't add a library. Don't fetch.
evals.expected_output: fullName (or equivalent) derived during render; no useEffect/useState copy of the name; no nested function component; lastName is used.
expectations: Renders firstName and lastName together (full name visible in the tree)
Does not use useEffect to copy first/last into state
Does not add useState whose only job is storing the concatenated name
Does not define a nested function component inside Profile
No extra util file or wrapper component file

evals.prompt: In settings.js, implement mergeSettings(raw) so a JSON string of user settings overlays defaults. Only theme and locale are allowed. Invalid JSON should fail. Don't add a library.
evals.expected_output: JSON.parse with failure on invalid JSON; allowlisted theme/locale; no Object.assign/merge of the parsed object (prototype pollution).
expectations: Invalid JSON is a failure the caller can observe (throw), not {}
Only theme and locale from the payload are applied — other keys ignored
Does not Object.assign(defaults, parsed) or lodash/recursive-merge the parsed object
Does not copy __proto__ / constructor / prototype from the payload onto defaults
Unknown or missing theme/locale keep the default (or fail if theme is an invalid value — either is ok)
No extra util file

evals.expected_output: AbortSignal or timeout; uses PRICES_URL not a caller URL; non-2xx is a failure before json(); invalid JSON fails; no [] on error.
expectations: Uses PRICES_URL — does not accept a caller-supplied URL
Outbound fetch has AbortSignal or an equivalent timeout
Non-2xx is a failure the caller can observe — not res.json() of a 500
Invalid JSON is a failure
Does not return [] or a placeholder list on any failure path
No empty catch that returns a default
No console.log leftovers

evals.prompt: In users.sql, add a statement that deactivates the user whose email is ada@example.com. Match the file. Don't add a framework.
evals.expected_output: UPDATE with WHERE on email (or id looked up by email); does not UPDATE/DELETE the whole table; no DROP.
expectations: Statement sets active to false (or equivalent deactivate) for ada@example.com
Has a WHERE that keys the row (email or id) — not a bare UPDATE/DELETE
Does not UPDATE or DELETE every row
Does not DROP TABLE / TRUNCATE
Does not invent columns that are not id/email/active/last_seen

evals.prompt: In app.py, add DELETE /items/{id} that deletes the current user's item. Reuse existing helpers. Don't add a framework.
evals.expected_output: Route uses Depends(get_current_user) and Depends(get_db) like get_item; store.delete_for with session user id; missing/other-owner fails; no module-global current_user.
expectations: DELETE /items/{id} exists
Uses Depends(get_current_user) — does not read a module-global current user
Uses Depends(get_db) or the existing store dependency — does not open a new global Session
Reuses delete_for (or equivalent scoped delete) so another owner's item fails
Missing or other-owner id is a failure the caller can observe (HTTPException or raise), not a 200 with {error}
No extra router/service file
